input: Opportunity: Explore why praise about a past experience does not necessarily reveal what led a couple to choose a wedding business, and how asking newly booked clients about that decision could inform advertising and landing-page messaging. Anchor the idea in Whitney’s proposed survey workflow, clearly presented as a proposal rather than a delivered service. | Audience: Wedding-business owners who have customer reviews but want a better understanding of what influences couples’ decisions. | Tension: A business may have plenty of positive feedback yet still lack direct information about why buyers selected it. | Argument: Reviews can tell a business what clients thought of their experience; asking newly booked clients what influenced their choice can surface a different kind of evidence, potentially useful when shaping ads and landing pages. | WIA expertise: Whitney distinguishes reviews from research into buying triggers and proposes surveys for newly booked clients, with responses shared for possible use in ad copy and landing pages. Fallon agrees the idea is worth exploring.
